text.p: Derlan Industries Ltd said on Thursday its Milton, Ontario-based aerospace division was awarded three contracts valued at C$17.6 million to manufacture helicopter transmissions and gear boxes.

Derlan, which manufactures products for the aerospace and industrial technologies sectors, said the largest of the three contracts, valued at C$9.3 million, calls for Derlan to supply Cincinnati-based GE Aircraft Engines with inlet gear boxes for the CFM56-5 engine. The engine is made by CFM International, a joint company of Snecma of France and General Electric Co. Delivery will start in 1997 and continue through 2000.

A second contract, valued at about C$3.9 million with GE Aircraft Engines, calls for Derlan to supply accessory gear boxes for General Electric's F110-100 engine, used on the U.S. military's F16 Falcon fighter jet. Delivery will begin before the end of 1997 and continue through 2000.

For the third contract, valued at about C$4.4 million, Derlan will supply the U.S. Army with 585 gears as spares for the UH60 Blackhawk helicopter. Delivery will begin in 1997 and continue through 1998.
